skill.name: error-tracking
skill.description: Guide for adding Sentry v8 error capture, performance spans, and service-specific monitoring patterns to Node.js services.
skill.summary: Adds Sentry v8 error tracking, performance monitoring, and testing patterns for application services.
skill.author: diet103

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript relative imports, localhost test commands, and normal Sentry configuration examples. One semantic privacy risk remains because the skill strongly encourages broad Sentry telemetry with user and workflow identifiers.

remediation.issue: Broad error capture can include personal or sensitive operational data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required redaction section that removes tokens, emails, request bodies, and sensitive identifiers before Sentry capture.

remediation.issue: Examples include user and workflow identifiers in error context.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify which identifiers are allowed, prefer stable pseudonymous IDs, and document data retention expectations.

remediation.issue: Local test endpoints can trigger deliberate errors in development services.
remediation.suggestion: State that curl examples must run only against local or approved test environments.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Error Telemetry Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires all errors to be captured in Sentry and shows user identifiers and workflow identifiers in error context. This can expose personal or sensitive operational data unless teams add strict redaction rules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly mandates Sentry capture and includes userId, instanceId, stepId, and entity-like workflow context. The skill also warns against sensitive data, so the risk is contextual rather than clearly malicious.

content.value_statement: Application teams need consistent error visibility across services. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Sentry v8 patterns for capture, context, and performance monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Shows controller, route, cron, workflow, and async operation error handling patterns.
Provides Sentry v8 initialization examples for form and notification services.
Defines performance monitoring patterns for database queries and custom spans.
Lists localhost test endpoints for validating error and performance capture.
Includes a checklist for adding Sentry coverage to new application code.
limitations: It is tailored to a specific service layout and may need path changes.
It assumes Sentry v8 and Node.js TypeScript service patterns.
It does not include automated code migration scripts.
Teams must add their own privacy review and data redaction rules.

use_cases.title: Instrument New API Controllers
use_cases.description: Add consistent Sentry capture and response handling when creating new Express controllers or routes.

use_cases.title: Monitor Background Jobs
use_cases.description: Add Sentry initialization, spans, and fatal error capture to cron jobs and workers.

use_cases.title: Review Observability Coverage
use_cases.description: Check services for missing Sentry setup, weak error context, and untracked slow database operations.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Error Capture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single route or controller method.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add Sentry error capture to this controller method. Keep existing behavior and avoid sensitive data in context.

prompt_templates.title: Instrument a Cron Job
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for background task monitoring.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to instrument this cron job with Sentry initialization, a cron span, captured exceptions, and safe shutdown behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Track Database Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for slow query visibility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to wrap these database calls with performance tracking and clear operation names. Include safe context only.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Service Observability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request across a service or feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review this service for Sentry gaps across controllers, workflows, cron jobs, and database operations. Return prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: A route catches errors with only console logging.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds Sentry exception capture, route tags, safe user context, and keeps the existing error response.

output_examples.input: A cron job exits after failures without telemetry.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds early Sentry initialization, a cron span, captured fatal errors, and completion logging.

output_examples.input: A database query sometimes takes several seconds.
output_examples.output: The assistant wraps the query in performance tracking and names the operation for Sentry analysis.

best_practices: Redact request bodies, tokens, emails, and secrets before sending error context to Sentry.
Use stable operation names and tags so teams can group related errors and spans.
Test error paths in local or approved test environments before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not send raw request payloads or credentials as Sentry context.
Do not rely on console errors when the service needs monitored failure reporting.
Do not add performance spans without clear names, owners, and sampling expectations.

faq.question: What does this skill help implement?
faq.answer: It helps implement Sentry v8 error capture, service initialization, performance spans, and testing patterns.

faq.question: Which services does the source document mention?
faq.answer: It mentions a form service and a notifications service, with separate Sentry setup examples.

faq.question: Does it run migration scripts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples for an assistant to apply in your codebase.

faq.question: Can it be used outside TypeScript services?
faq.answer: Some concepts transfer, but the examples are written for Node.js and TypeScript services.

faq.question: What data should be excluded from Sentry context?
faq.answer: Exclude secrets, tokens, passwords, full request bodies, emails, and regulated personal data.

faq.question: Is Sentry configuration included?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes DSN, environment, trace sampling, profiling, and database monitoring examples.
